chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'What is your view if I needed a physician and he was a Christian, should I greet him with peace and supplicate for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indeed your supplication will not benefit him.'
ai.seo_question: Should I greet a non-Muslim doctor with peace and pray for him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) permits greeting and supplicating for a Christian physician, illustrating the Shia principle of *adab* (etiquette) in professional interactions regardless of the recipient's faith. The Imam’s clarification that the supplication 'does not benefit him' (*la yanfa'uhu*) is interpreted by scholars as referring to the specific context of the supplication or the individual's spiritual state, rather than negating the virtue of the act itself, thereby balancing social courtesy with theological precision.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if I was needy to the physician and he was a Christian, should I greet (السَّلَامُ) upon him and supplicate for him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, (but) your supplication will not benefit him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “

Once I asked abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) ‘If 1 needed to visit a Christian physician, can I offer him the greeting of peace and pray for him?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, but your prayer will not benefit him.’”
